subject: science
cluster: Stars, the Sun, and patterns in the sky
skillName: Why the Sun Looks Brighter Than Other Stars
intro: The Sun is a star, just like the stars we see at night. The Sun looks far brighter and bigger than any other star because it is much, much closer to Earth. The other stars are enormous and give off huge amounts of light, but they are so extremely far away that they look like tiny, dim points. If the Sun were as far away as those stars, it would also look like a small dim point. So the difference in brightness we see is mainly caused by differences in distance, not because the Sun is special among stars.

items.prompt: Why does the Sun look so much brighter than the stars we see at night?

steps: The Sun is a star, like the others.
The Sun is extremely close to Earth compared to all other stars.
Because it is so much closer, it appears far brighter than the distant stars.
solution.answer: Because the Sun is much closer to Earth than the other stars, so it appears far brighter.

items.prompt: A student sees two identical flashlights, one nearby and one far down a field. The near one looks much brighter. How does this model why the Sun looks brighter than other stars?

steps: Both flashlights give off the same amount of light, just like stars can be similar.
The closer flashlight looks brighter only because it is nearer.
In the same way, the Sun looks brighter than other stars mainly because it is much closer to Earth.
solution.answer: Like the closer flashlight, the Sun looks brighter mainly because it is closer, not because it gives off more light than every other star.

items.prompt: A classmate argues the Sun is the brightest object because it is the biggest star. Use the idea of distance to give a better argument.

steps: Many stars are actually as big as or bigger than the Sun.
Those stars look dim only because they are extremely far away.
So the Sun looks brightest mainly because it is the closest star, not because it is the biggest.
solution.answer: The Sun looks brightest mainly because it is the closest star; other stars are large too but look dim due to great distance.

items.prompt: Is the Sun a star? Explain.

steps: Stars are giant glowing balls of hot gas that give off light.
The Sun is a giant glowing ball of hot gas that gives off light, so the Sun is a star.
solution.answer: Yes, the Sun is a star.

items.prompt: If the Sun were moved as far away as other stars, how would it look from Earth?

steps: Moving the Sun extremely far away would make it look much dimmer.
From Earth it would then look like a tiny dim point, just like the other stars.
solution.answer: It would look like a tiny, dim point of light, just like the other stars.

items.prompt: Two stars give off the same amount of light, but one looks brighter from Earth. What can you conclude about their distances?

steps: If two stars give off equal light, the brighter-looking one must be affected by distance.
A closer star looks brighter than a farther one that gives off the same light.
So the brighter-looking star is closer to Earth.
solution.answer: The star that looks brighter is closer to Earth.
